subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures preserve the asynchronous accepted `sessions_spawn` response and then terminalize visibly, or should OpenClaw preflight enough sandbox startup work to reject before returning accepted?
rationale: The choice affects the public async spawn contract, session/subagent state, gateway waits, and the overlapping lifecycle work, so automation should not pick the permanent behavior alone.

options.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add visible logged terminal startup failure state in session history, subagent list, and agent waits.

options.title: Preflight Sandbox Before Accept
options.body: Move enough sandbox startup validation before the accepted response to fail fast, accepting extra spawn latency and compatibility review.

options.title: Resolve Through Lifecycle Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers settle the broader lifecycle event contract and then apply the sandbox-specific Docker proof.

recommendation.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add visible logged terminal startup failure state in session history, subagent list, and agent waits.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history ties steipete to both `sessions_spawn` sandbox inheritance and subagent spawn contract work.
